answers.text: After QQQ gaps down 1% or more, how often does it fill the gap the same day?
answers.reply: Here is how I read that question.  On QQQ, 220 of the 559 sessions that met the condition (1999-03-10 to 2026-11-25) saw the outcome - price reached prev_close - a historical frequency of 39.4% (95% confidence interval 35.4% to 43.5%). Across all 6,972 evaluated sessions the same outcome occurred 66.9% of the time, so the condition lowers it by 27.5 percentage points; the difference is statistically distinguishable from the other sessions (p < 0.001). After the starting point the average best move was +1.85% and the average worst move -1.48%; the horizon ended +0.16% on average and higher on 50.8% of sessions. Where intraday bars exist, the target was typically reached 157 min after the start. These are underlying price statistics, not option returns, and past frequency is not a forecast. QQQ trades back to the previous close (the gap fills) on 220 of 559 days when it opened 1% or more below the previous close (39.4%). There is no fair "any day" comparison for this: on days without the condition the price starts at that level, so reaching it is automatic. Allowing for how few days there are, the true rate is likely between 35.4% and 43.5%. 559 Days that matched your rules 220 Days it happened 339 Days it didn't

answers.text: Does the first 15-minute candle predict the rest of SPY's session?
answers.reply: Research plan: 2 related configurations will be run and compared with their baselines. On every SPY session with intraday bars: the direction of the first 15 minutes (close against the open) is compared with the direction of the rest of the session (the candle's close to the session's close). Up and down candles are counted separately, each against all sessions.  The direction of SPY's first 15 minutes and the direction of the rest of the session: from the end of the candle to the close it matched on 50.4%, against 50.1% for unrelated directions: that is no more than chance produces. First 15 minutes: matched the rest of the session (09:45 to the close) on 50.4% of 2,731 sessions (95% interval 48.5% to 52.3%; 50.1% if unrelated). The first 15-minute candle matched the direction of the rest of the session 50.4% of the time, about what two unrelated directions would give. If the two directions were unrelated they would match about 50.1% of the time; the measured rate's likely range is 48.5% to 52.3%.
